messages.author: c9416b6005bf4eb7
messages.subject: GSOC-R 2021
parts:
Hi all, happy new year, this is a reminder about the upcoming GSOC-R 2021.

ADMINS we will need to submit an org application sometime between Jan 29 and Feb 19. In previous years I have done this and I can do it again, but I was wondering if one of the other/new admins would be interested to learn how? If so you can start with these answers from last year and you can ask me if you need any help.
https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/Admin-application

MENTORS we need your help to populate https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects with project ideas before our org app submission. I have added a few ideas and already received some contact/interest from students. I encourage potential mentors to start posting project ideas now, with a soft deadline end Jan and a hard deadline end of Feb.

Hi James, thanks for contributing a project idea and welcome to the R-GSOC mentors family!
To be clear you do not need to join the ADMIN team if you want to be a mentor. Joining the ADMIN team is an informal process that typical happens after actively contributing to R-GSOC for some time. (we should probably write an official policy document about this but so far there is none)

messages.subject: Re: GSOC-R 2021
parts:
Toby, 

I've been a mentor for a few years now. Project-wise, I mentored:
- unofficially, 2017:  the sparse matrix extension to RcppArmadillo in 2018
- officially, 2018: Vowpal Wabbit rewrite (rvw).
- 2019: there was a hiccup with due-dates, so the `mlpack` project wasn't eligible under the R organization.
- 2020: I mentored the R project bindings with the mlpack org. 

Best,

JJB
